item.title: AI and the future of shopping: are we ready for what’s coming?
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes looks at the new trend of surveillance shopping. AI can now predict when and where we plan to spend our hard-earned bucks. Stores can take that information and change prices on an hourly basis to maximize profit. But is this an unfair strategy, one that is harmful to the consumer? And is it even legal? Or is this a future inevitability that we all have to accept? Joining Scottie for this conversation are Dr. Tamara Patzer, author and creator at the Daily Success Media Network, and Michael Wynne, an attorney who focuses on US federal criminal investigations and trials.

item.title: Dying off: Can congressional term limits save the American republic?
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes examines the average and growing age of American politicians. Recent examples of politicians withering into old age while in office include Dianne Feinstein, Joe Biden, and Mitch McConnell. So, should the US enact term limits at the federal and state levels? Or would this lead to the few actually competent leaders we have being run out of office before their time? Joining the conversation are John Pudner, President of Freedom and Family Action, and Carson Carpenter, host of The Common Cause.

item.title: Neighbor wars: US-Canada trade disagreements spill over into regional struggle
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes looks at the growing trade war between the United States and Canada as we celebrate Labor Day in the US. Canada relies on the US much more than the other way around. Yet the US consumer could still feel the pinch if this drags out much longer. What will it take to make a deal? David Morgan of the Morgan Report and independent journalist Kat Kanada join Scottie for this discussion. Don’t miss it!

item.title: Trump and the rotating cast of British prime ministers
item.description: The UK seems to go through prime ministers like a chameleon changes its colors, but it doesn’t seem to faze Donald Trump. One thing that doesn’t change, however, is the UK’s hard line against Russia in the conflict with Ukraine. So, will Andy Burnham continue to thwart President Trump’s peace plans? And what happens if the US tells the UK and Europe to go it alone in their support of Ukraine? Join this conversation with David Vance, independent political commentator, and Hussain Shafiei, British politician.

item.title: The GOP is looking to win the midterms
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes discusses the recent RNC midterm convention. Usually conventions are only held in presidential election years. But this time Trump and MAGA are looking to reinvigorate the party as it stares down the barrel of the gun of Democrats flipping both the House and Senate. Can the GOP parry the blow and keep at least the Senate and maybe both chambers, or will the legislative branch be stripped from the president’s grasp? Joining Scottie for this discussion are conservative pundit Steve Malzberg and the host of the Mike Schwartz show, Mike Schwartz.

item.title: The Curse of the Bearded Lady
item.description: On this episode of America First , Scottie Nell Hughes is joined by author and commentator A.J. Rice. The two discuss Rice’s new book, ‘The Curse of the Bearded Lady’, and the way the trans agenda has shaped so much of American cultural discourse over the past decade. Is the tide turning and is the woke movement finally on its deathbed, or are we doomed to deal with bearded ladies for the foreseeable future? Don’t miss it!

item.title: The Greenland deal: US moving in on the Arctic
item.description: US President Donald Trump got his way on the Greenland deal. Denmark and the island have signed an agreement to allow the United States to expand its military presence there. So, what does that mean for the Arctic region and the American relationship with Europe? Join us for that conversation with guests Karen Kwiatkowski, former US Air Force Officer, and David Pyne, Deputy Executive Director of the Task Force on National & Homeland Security.
